title: A method for soil moisture probes calibration and validation of satellite estimates
author: Holzman, Rivas, et al.

steps.title: Select sampling sites and soil types
steps.instruction: Choose four representative parcels (two in Córdoba province and two in Buenos Aires province) covering the soil types listed in Table 1: Sample 1 (Typic Haplustoll, loam 22 % clay / 46 % silt / 32 % sand, OM 2.2 %), Sample 2 (Typic Argiudoll, clay loam 29 % clay / 45 % silt / 26 % sand, OM 3.0 %), Sample 3 (Typic Argiudoll, loam 24 % clay / 39 % silt / 37 % sand, OM 5.4 %), and Sample 4 (Typic Argiudoll, silty loam 25 % clay / 51 % silt / 24 % sand, OM 4.8 %). Record latitude/longitude for each parcel as given.

steps.title: Perform handheld probe measurements along transects
steps.instruction: At SMOS overpass time, lay out three parallel transects across each parcel. In each transect, a team walks the transect, taking a Delta‑T thetaProbe ML2x measurement every 10 m for about 15 min, first moving toward the parcel centre and then branching at 90° in opposite directions until the parcel limit. Collect roughly 30 measurements per transect. Note that the probe accuracy is ±0.05 m³ m⁻³ (0‑70 °C) with the supplied calibration, and after soil‑type calibration ±0.01 m³ m⁻³ (0‑40 °C) or ±0.02 m³ m⁻³ (40‑70 °C).

steps.title: Collect undisturbed soil cores
steps.instruction: From each parcel, extract a 10 cm‑deep undisturbed soil sample using a metal cylinder of known volume: radius = 4.9 cm, height ≈ 10.7 cm, giving a volume of ≈ 800 cm³. After insertion, cut the cylinder at its base and seal both ends to prevent loss of material.

steps.title: Seal cores and transport to laboratory
steps.instruction: Close the base of each cylinder with a paper (or metal) filter that permits only downward water movement. Keep the probe fixed inside the core throughout handling to avoid disturbance, then transport the sealed cores to the lab.

steps.title: Saturate cores and begin ambient drying
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, fully saturate each core with water. Afterwards, allow the cores to dry freely at ambient temperature (≈ 20 °C) by natural evaporation.

steps.title: Daily weigh cores and record probe readings
steps.instruction: Each day, weigh the entire assembly (cylinder + soil + probe) and record the weight. Simultaneously, read the volumetric water content (θᵥ) from the ML2x probe (which remains fixed inside the core). Continue daily measurements until the weight remains constant for three consecutive days, indicating the end of the free‑drying phase.

steps.title: Determine dry mass by oven drying
steps.instruction: Remove the cores from the ambient‑drying stage and place them in an oven at 105 °C for 48 h. After cooling, weigh the cylinder + probe again and subtract this weight to obtain the dry soil mass (Mₛ).

steps.title: Calculate bulk density and reference water content
steps.instruction: Compute bulk density (ρ_b) for each sample as ρ_b = Mₛ / V_t, where V_t is the known cylinder volume (≈ 800 cm³). Then calculate the reference volumetric water content using θ_v = (M_t − Mₛ) / Mₛ × ρ_b / ρ_w, where M_t is the mass of soil plus water measured during the free‑drying phase and ρ_w is the density of water.

steps.title: Derive calibration equations for each probe
steps.instruction: Compare the reference θᵥ values with the corresponding ML2x probe readings for each soil type. Perform linear regression to obtain calibration equations, and compute performance metrics (RMSE and bias) for each probe‑soil combination.

steps.title: Validate calibration with independent dataset
steps.instruction: Apply the derived calibration equations to a separate set of measurements (n = 33). Calculate post‑calibration RMSE and bias to assess accuracy; values lower than the manufacturer’s ±0.05 m³ m⁻³ specification indicate successful calibration.
